Third Sunday in Ordinary Time September 6 2026 This weekend September 12th 13th the Church celebrates the Twenty fourth Sunday in Ordinary Time Our readings focus on one of the most difficult demands of Christian discipleship forgiveness Jesus tells us of the parable of the servant who refuses to forgive the small debt of another after he has been forgiven a great debt Sirach likewise warns that we cannot ask God for mercy if we are unwilling to show mercy ourselves The lesson is clear the mercy we seek from God must become the mercy we extend to others Each of us stands before God like the servant whose unpayable debt has been erased Every time we approach Confession we receive an act of mercy greater than we can comprehend How then can we accept such forgiveness while withholding it from others including those who have hurt us Forgiveness does not excuse wrongdoing or erase every consequence but it does surrender our desire for revenge and entrust justice to God The forgiven Christian must become a forgiving Christian Discover Catholicism As a reminder this weekly series on Thursdays at 6:30PM in the Parish Conference Room is open to all If you or someone you know is interested in this series and in joining the Catholic Church this coming year but our Thursday time does not work for their calendar please have them contact me through the Parish Office We will do everything possible for those desiring to formally enter the Church to make sure their preparation can move forward Upcoming Events Though it often seems that September slows down as we enter into the Fall and schools resume we actually have a number of special events quickly coming up This Tuesday September 15th you are invited to join us at 6 PM either for our Ask Father Series in the Parish Conference Room or to be trained as a Lector for our weekend Masses in the Church The following week we join our community in celebrating the annual Bluffton Free Street Fair As in past years our parish will have our annual informational table out in the streets If you are interested in helping to staff the table at any time throughout the week please let me know It's always a wonderful opportunity to be present amount of community pray with visitors and answer questions about our Catholic Faith The week after Street Fair will hopefully be a time of a transition as we prepare for the long awaited re opening of our sanctuary for the following weekend During this time we will need volunteers to help clean move and rearrange our liturgical furnishings and restock our sacristies for liturgical use Watch for volunteer sheets in the coming weeks to help with this work Entering into October we have a number of events all in a row For the first weekend of October we will have Stuff the Truck to support the St Vincent de Paul Thriftstore in nearby Huntington donations accepted on our campus Saturday October 3rd through Sunday October 4th our annual St Francis Blessing of Animals Saturday October 3rd at Noon and our annual Parish Picnic on Sunday October 4th following the 10 AM Mass Our Knights of Columbus are once again leading our local Days of Caring in mid October This event welcomes a number of local churches coming together and volunteering at several charities right here in our community We ll also have several fun fraternal events from a parish Board Game Night to an Open Gym to a Trivia Night throughout October Looking even further ahead we will host at least two concerts in the newly renovated Church have an Advent Mission with a speaker from the Fathers of Mercy our annual Parish Forty Hours and a number of other events This is all in addition to our normal parish schedule from daily Mass times for both adoration and confession our Knights of Columbus our GIRL's Night Out choir practices Discover Catholicism etc Needless to say we have a busy year ahead Let's plan for it and make the most of it together Saturday September 12 400 4:45pm
